chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan, he said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:

Some people asked me about a man who spent a night from the nights of Mina in Mecca, so I said: I do not know. Then I said to him: May I be your ransom, what do you say about it? He said: There is a blood-guilt (dam) on him if he spent the night. I said: If his staying was due to the matter he was engaged in from his tawaf and sa'i, and it was not for sleep or pleasure, is there upon him the same as upon this one? He said: This is not in the same position as that one, and I do not like for the dawn to break for him except while he is in Mina.

key_terms.دَم: Dam, a sacrificial offering or blood-guilt incurred for missing a ritual obligation
key_terms.سَعْي: Sa'i, the ritual walking between Safa and Marwa
key_terms.طَوَاف: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.لَيْلَات مِنًى: The nights of Mina (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims spend the nights of Tashriq

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who stays in Mecca instead of Mina during the nights of Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who spends the night in Mecca instead of Mina, distinguishing between necessity and preference. He rules that if the stay is due to the necessity of ritual acts like tawaf and sa'i, it is excused, but if it is for sleep or pleasure, it incurs a blood-guilt (dam). The Imam expresses a strong preference that dawn should not break for the pilgrim except while they are in Mina, highlighting the importance of the Mina stay as a core pillar of Hajj.
